The portable protocol and suppliers live in
`packages/utils/src/internal-accounts/employee-address-migration*.ts`.
Infrastructure retains compatible re-exports. Web owns POST endpoints under
`/api/v1/infrastructure/internal-accounts/address-migrations/{inspect,prepare,migrate}`.
The Infrastructure internal-accounts page exposes their operator dialog through
`@tuturuuu/internal-api/infrastructure`. Runtime availability follows current root
administrator permission, valid server configuration and fresh SQL/provider
readiness. No optional migration activation environment variable is consulted;
an absent or false `EMPLOYEE_ADDRESS_MIGRATION_RUNTIME_ENABLED` does not disable
an otherwise authorized operation. CI qualification selections below remain
independently opt-in test controls. Account execution still needs the operator's
authorized exact tuple and the operation's one-attempt protocol.

## Explicit operator preparation and recovery

In Infrastructure's internal-accounts dialog, enter the target UUID and exact
legacy source address. For an existing intent, also enter its original operation
UUID **before the first action**. Leave the operation field blank only for a new
intent. The first inspect or preparation persists and freezes the operation UUID,
target, both addresses and revision zero. Denial does not unlock or discard them.
The original operation remains available through close/reopen and remount within
the same actor/workspace browser session. Unavailable or malformed recovery
storage fails closed; do not replace an uncertain operation to bypass recovery.
A new session with no stored receipt starts in editing state.

Use **Confirm and prepare mailbox once** only as a separately authorized action.
Retype the exact target UUID and both addresses. This uses the typed existing
prepare POST with the account-action header and unchanged server authorization,
origin and permission checks. A preparation receipt means mailbox preparation
was acknowledged, never that account migration completed. Inspect the same
operation afterwards. Retype both addresses for migration; the session performs
another fresh inspection before its sole migration request.

Version 2 browser receipts record the exact tuple and an unattempted, prepared,
uncertain-inspection, uncertain-preparation or migration-dispatched phase.
Legacy bare tuples remain compatible and conservatively inspect-only. An unknown
preparation outcome cannot be replayed, including after denied, forbidden or
invalid inspections. Only exact authoritative readiness may unlock migration;
preparation never becomes eligible again. Before any preparation, a known
not-ready/conflict inspection may allow explicit preparation, while a pre-read
forbidden/invalid response retains the unknown-inspection fence. A dispatched
migration can only be inspected, regardless of later ready/denied replies. Transport errors and malformed acknowledgements do
not establish readiness or completion. The UI does not retry either write.

Focused coverage lives in Infrastructure's `address-migration-session.test.ts`
and `address-migration-dialog.test.tsx`, and internal-api's
`employee-address-migration.test.ts`. They cover exact preparation confirmation,
known-operation recovery, denied/remounted tuple retention, legacy receipts,
unknown outcomes, actor retirement, receipt validation and fresh migration
preflight. Synthetic tests do not establish production mailbox delivery or
customer identity/data preservation. Run them from their owning app/package using
the currently admitted resource route; do not activate or rewrite shared shims to
obtain local admission. Exact-commit CI and authorized customer acceptance remain
separate evidence.

## Address and identity policy

The operation changes a canonical lowercase managed-subdomain address
to the same localpart at exactly `tuturuuu.com`. It rejects external domains,
root-address sources, a changed localpart, self-action, unknown ownership,
conflicting reservations, stale revisions and unverified source identities.
It never requests another Auth UUID, account creation/deletion, password,
metadata, administrator grants or ban changes. The bounded Google destination
transition below is the sole exception to the email-only confirmation policy.
The provider port exposes only a read and an email update on the original UUID.

A protected journal supplier must reauthorize the confirmed active root
administrator and lock/revalidate the original actor, UUID, both addresses and
all competing CREATE/RESTORE/migration reservations in every transaction. The
supplier must independently observe real Auth/provider identity IDs, the public
identity, workspace memberships, grants, saved data and mailbox routes. A caller
supplied boolean or fingerprint is not administrator or preservation proof.
Fingerprints must use documented canonical snapshots and must exclude only the
specific email fields that this operation is allowed to change.

## Persisted operation protocol

An original operation UUID binds the actor, target UUID, source/destination,
revision, immutable-state fingerprint and provider-identity fingerprint.
Reservation must be durably idempotent on that whole binding, with unique
unresolved target/address ownership. An atomic attempt claim returns true to
exactly one invocation; every replay returns false. Neither lease expiry nor
process restart may reissue that claim. Attempt IDs are server-generated UUIDs.

The executor requires an independent committed read after reservation, attempt
claim and completion. A claimed attempt also needs its one-time acknowledgement;
a persisted attempted row alone cannot authorize another provider request.
Crashes and lost responses retain the original operation for inspection. Even a
reserved replay is inspection-only. No expiry, replacement operation, rollback,
compensation or automatic provider retry is part of this contract.

A provider email update must use the supported admin update on the original UUID
with `{ email }` for the original email-provider path. It must perform one request without transport retry and
preserve existing provider identity IDs. Actual GoTrue behavior, verification
challenges, secure-email-change settings and concurrent external administrators
must be qualified before activating that supplier. An unverified destination or
changed identity remains pending. Only the separately qualified Google destination
transition may request `email_confirm: true`, backed by the exact verified claim.

Inspection can complete a named attempted operation after observing the verified
destination and unchanged identity. Completion must independently verify actual
Auth state and preservation, then atomically update only approved registry/public
email projections and mailbox routing with a revision increment. The final
readback must match the original binding, completed phase and exact next revision.
A completed replay returns that original receipt without another provider write.

## Evidence and remaining gates

`employee-address-migration.test.ts` exercises the real source executor with an
explicitly in-memory journal/provider fixture. It covers concurrent callers,
strict old/new tuples, lost reserve/claim/provider acknowledgements, false
acknowledgements, source/destination verification, identity drift, immutable-state
drift, completed replay and inspection without relaunch.

This fixture does **not** establish durable persistence, SQL lock/ACL behavior,
real email change/verification, mailbox delivery, public profile convergence or
UUID/membership/data preservation in a real project. Those remain supplier gates.
The additive `20261017010000_employee_address_migrations.sql` supplier implements
service-only journal transactions with direct table access revoked, durable
unique target/address reservations and a one-time claim. Its scope is deliberately
legacy accounts absent from CREATE/RESTORE registries with email-provider-only
identities, first revision zero to one.
The original email-v1 path requires existing active source and destination mailboxes and matching active
domains, with both mailboxes owned exclusively by the target UUID. It does not
provision mail, change addresses on mailboxes, set onboarding metadata or convert
the account into the CREATE registry. The retained completed migration is its
address registry; the existing Auth synchronization trigger owns the public email
projection. A missing route or registry conflict fails closed.

The immutable snapshot covers Auth password/metadata/ban/role/phone state, the
public profile, private details except email projections, workspace memberships,
workspace role assignments/definitions/permissions, platform grants, owned
mailboxes, mailbox memberships and the two domains. It hashes these protected
values without returning the snapshot. Saved application rows remain linked to
the unchanged UUID; this is not an exhaustive snapshot of every application table.
Migration transactions first try exclusive global address admission without
waiting. Busy admission raises SQLSTATE `55P03` before any capability or state
change; it must not queue behind a shared writer and block later shared writers.
Guarded ordinary writers take shared admission before statement row locks. This avoids
the destination-row/advisory inversion without serializing ordinary writers with
each other. Both original and destination addresses remain reserved permanently.
Both RPCs and guarded writers require READ COMMITTED isolation. The RPC uses
NOWAIT for row and authorization-table locks after admission; contention aborts
without issuing a claim, releasing admission for existing CREATE/RESTORE/provider
transactions that already hold rows. There is no automatic retry. Authorization dependencies use
short transaction SHARE locks to fence concurrent
permission revocation and absent-row grant changes. Qualification must measure
that lock scope before activation. Reservation triggers also fence Auth users and
identities, public email profiles, mailboxes, reserved grants and CREATE intents.

The identity fingerprint is lowercase SHA-256 of compact UTF-8 JSON tuples
`[[identity_id, provider, user_id], ...]`, sorted by canonical UUID `identity_id`.
GoTrue JSON `identity_id` maps to SQL `auth.identities.id`; JSON `id` is the
provider-specific ID. SQL explicitly constructs compact JSON under C collation.
Email fields are excluded so the original identity remains recognizable.

The original email-v1 provider uses the installed supported `auth.admin.updateUserById(id, {email})`
contract. Its independent verification requires the matching email identity's
`email_verified=true`, the confirmed timestamp, no pending email and an active
account. Upstream GoTrue's admin email-only path can set identity verification
false while retaining the confirmed timestamp. That observation stays pending;
there is no confirmation override or automatic retry. See the
[GoTrue admin handler](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/v2.197.0/internal/api/admin.go#L235-L284)
and [supported JavaScript API](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-admin-updateuserbyid).

The disposable SQL qualification runner exercises the actual migration on an
isolated PostgreSQL fixture with explicitly reduced prerequisite tables. It is
not a full migration-history replay or a real GoTrue provider result. It includes
a three-session blocking-exclusive control and all four RPC actions under shared
contention, checking `55P03`, unrelated Auth-writer progress and unchanged fixture
state. Competing claims are drained without retry; exactly one successful
capability must match the durable journal attempt and independent inspection.
The loser may return false or the exact owned SQLSTATE `55P03` admission-busy
envelope; other errors fail qualification. The 10-assertion composed SQL packet
does not run these concurrency cases.
Run it only with separate admission for its disposable database lifecycle, via
the canonical resource queue:

```sh
ttr resources run -- node apps/database/scripts/employee-address-migration-qualification.mjs
```

The runner retains the exact observed daemon identity
`docker-desktop linux 29.8.2` as a pre-creation admission fence. This identifies
the originally targeted local fixture; it is not a PostgreSQL compatibility
requirement or approval for another daemon/version. A mismatch requires a
separately reviewed target/admission decision, not removal of the check.

A separate real-provider runner uses cached GoTrue `v2.197.0` and PostgreSQL
`17.11.0.004` images on an internal Docker network without published ports.
GoTrue distinguishes user confirmation from identity verification:
[admin creation](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/v2.197.0/internal/api/admin.go#L473-L528)
creates the email identity with the default false verification claim, then
[confirms the user](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/v2.197.0/internal/models/user.go#L488-L507).
Magic-link OTP uses recovery verification, which does not update that identity
flag. The installed SDK forwards these fields; it does not repair the mismatch.
The Utils transport regression owns an SDK devDependency at the existing locked
version. Its strict isolated dependency layout must resolve that import directly;
a hoisted root SDK can mask a missing package declaration during local checks.
A confirmed timestamp plus correlated email alone therefore does not satisfy this
migration's stricter verification contract. The guard remains unchanged.

The positive fixture creates an unconfirmed disposable source and uses supported
`generateLink({type: 'signup', ...})` followed by signup `verifyOtp`.
[Signup verification](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/v2.197.0/internal/api/verify.go#L294-L375)
sets the matching identity flag through GoTrue. This fixture path is not a repair
procedure for already-confirmed legacy accounts; generating a signup link for
an already-confirmed user is rejected by the pinned server.

The real supplier then issues one email-only PUT on that UUID. The runner drops
the successful response to exercise an unknown acknowledgement, reads back the
actual destination, and proves protocol replay and a repeated supplier call do
not issue another PUT. UUID, identity IDs, password hash, metadata, ban state,
confirmation timestamp, sessions and refresh-token rows are compared privately.
A separate fixture-owned mail table is also compared; that table does not prove
preservation of the full product mail schema or hosted delivery. The journal is
an explicit fixture. The destination identity becomes unverified, so the result
remains `pending` for inspection; this is positive provider mutation and
preservation qualification, not a completed address migration.

```sh
ttr resources run -- bun apps/database/scripts/employee-address-migration-gotrue-qualification.ts --source=signup
```

The retained negative mode creates the source with admin confirmation and uses
magic-link OTP. It must remain unverified under the stricter contract, refuse the
supplier change with zero PUTs, and preserve its original snapshot:

```sh
ttr resources run -- bun apps/database/scripts/employee-address-migration-gotrue-qualification.ts --source=magiclink
```

The full-schema workflow's separate `include_address_migration=true` selection
adds `employee-address-migration.sql` with exactly 10 rollback assertions. It
qualifies the legacy SQL path and existing profile trigger, without treating SQL
simulation as real GoTrue verification. Foundation and journal receipts remain
incompatible and keep their original defaults; see the
[qualification profiles](./employee-schema-qualification).

Before release, apply the full schema in the approved isolated fixture,
verify generated types, real GoTrue and Web transport behavior, hosted mail routing,
and the exact Web/Infrastructure builds in CI. Existing schema CI guards remain
in force; a reduced fixture never replaces that gate. Record a scoped
promotion/rollback plan separately. CREATE or RESTORE receipts do not qualify
this migration, and production/provider/SQL actions require separate authority.


## Permission-authorized Web and Infrastructure surface

The surface currently admits only canonical `@xwf.tuturuuu.com` sources and the
same localpart at `@tuturuuu.com`. Its initial expected revision is zero, matching
the supplier's legacy-first scope. It cannot adopt CREATE/RESTORE registry rows,
repair identity verification, provision mailboxes or bypass ownership readiness.
For the original email-v1 path, both approved active mailboxes must already belong to the original user. The separately bounded Google-destination exception is described below.

Every invocation uses the existing Infrastructure satellite/request-session
root-admin authorizer, with a confirmed active exact root-domain actor and
`manage_internal_accounts`. The client never supplies that actor. POSTs require
the account-action header, same-origin browser origin/fetch-site checks and
strict bounded JSON. Each RPC/provider boundary and successful disclosure
rechecks the original actor. Composition and reauthorization have no optional
migration activation flag; current permissions remain authoritative.

Inspection returns readiness only after fresh committed SQL and verified active
provider observations agree on the exact original tuple and fingerprints. It
projects no fingerprint to the browser. The dialog requires both exact addresses,
then repeats inspection before the single explicit migration invocation. That
invocation still performs the supplier's own fresh admission checks. A successful
mutation reply alone does not publish completion in the UI: a separate inspection
must confirm the original operation, target UUID and destination.

Before migration dispatch, the browser retains the original operation UUID,
revision and tuple in actor/workspace-scoped session recovery. Closing/reopening
or remounting keeps that recovery; switching actor/workspace retires in-flight
callbacks and prevents disclosure or another dispatch from the old lifetime.
Uncertain replies, unavailable readiness, pending verification and lost
acknowledgements remain inspectable. No retry, replacement UUID, password/token
entry, provider compensation or fabricated success is offered. Session recovery
is local to that browser tab; the server journal remains authoritative.

Focused regressions cover real Web adapter/provider/journal composition using
synthetic transport observations, typed-client tuple validation and UI/controller
lifetime/recovery behavior. They do not qualify hosted sessions, full schema,
mail delivery, actual account preservation or production completion. Keep the
supplier qualification gates and exact Web/Infrastructure CI builds separate.

## Verified Google destination and explicit mailbox preparation

The forward migration `20261019010000_employee_google_destination_migration.sql`
adds a narrow legacy compatibility path. The source must be a confirmed, active,
nonanonymous UUID with exactly one Google identity whose provider ID equals its
nonempty subject, whose email is the exact canonical destination, and whose
`email_verified` claim is exactly true. The legacy Auth/public email may still be
at the source. A verified source-address Google claim does not qualify this path.
No upstream Google account change, identity rewrite or manufactured claim occurs.

The administrator first explicitly POSTs the original operation/UUID/address/
revision tuple to `/api/v1/infrastructure/internal-accounts/address-migrations/prepare`,
with the same request authentication, origin and account-action header used by
migration. This is an administrative mutation, not an inspection operation.
It can adopt only an existing canonical personal mailbox that has NULL creator,
`disabled` status, no archive timestamp, an active canonical domain and zero
members or foreign-key-referenced data/configuration. Quarantined, archived,
shared, owned, populated or conflicting mailboxes fail closed. It creates no
legacy route and changes no Auth or Google state. NOWAIT admission, actor/target
locks, membership-table and referencing-table locks fence concurrent changes;
contention is a failure, never an automatic retry. Every existing migration
record for the target/address prevents preparation, including another operation
UUID. The endpoint requires a separate committed inspection before acknowledging
preparation. Unknown preparation outcomes require inspection, not blind retry.

After preparation, independently inspect the same original tuple. Only then may
migration reserve a fresh persisted snapshot and claim its single attempt.
Inspection remains unavailable while the mailbox is inactive or unowned.
For this exact Google shape, the provider makes one supported admin request
`{ email: destination, email_confirm: true }`. The confirmation comes from the
already verified exact Google destination claim, with fresh authorization and
source readback; timestamps alone cannot authorize it. The original Google
identity ID, provider ID, subject and complete identity data remain fixed.
GoTrue may add exactly one verified email identity for the same UUID/destination;
no other provider/identity addition, removal or change is accepted.

The original binding and snapshot stay immutable. The journal independently
observes the actual post identity and state hashes, verifies that removing only
that new email identity reconstructs the protected original snapshot, and stores
a distinct before/after transition receipt in its completion transaction. The
executor independently compares the provider's actual post hash and requires the
persisted receipt on final readback. It never treats the original and new hashes
as equal. Unknown provider outcomes retain the original attempt for inspection;
inspection and replay cannot issue another provider request.

The separate rollback packet `employee-google-destination-migration.sql` has
exactly 30 assertions and is selected by the existing default-off address-migration
qualification profile. The original 10-assertion packet and default foundation172/
journal301 profiles remain intact; opting into both address packets yields 212
or 341 assertions respectively. The real-provider runner has a separate mode:

```sh
ttr resources run -- bun apps/database/scripts/employee-address-migration-gotrue-qualification.ts --source=google-destination
```

That mode seeds synthetic Google claims in a disposable database and exercises
real pinned GoTrue admin behavior with a lost acknowledgement. It does not prove
external Google sign-in, hosted mailbox delivery or the application SQL journal.
The Web state-flow fixture also uses synthetic SQL observations. Require the
new packet on the full isolated schema, real-provider mode, generated types,
exact-commit Web/Infrastructure builds, and independent source review before
release. This source candidate does not authorize production preparation or Auth
writes. Mail delivery and actual customer account preservation remain separate
post-release checks owned by the authorized operator.


### Real-provider preservation and the optional CI hook

The Google provider mode first signs in the disposable confirmed password source
and independently reads its authenticated user, then seeds the synthetic Google
claim. Its baseline requires nonempty persisted sessions and refresh tokens,
including an unrevoked token, before the single admin email update. Every column
of those persisted rows is compared afterward alongside the original Google row,
UUID, password, metadata and mail fixture. Four controls delete or mutate observed
session/token rows and require the same preservation assertion to fail; they do
not modify the fixture database. Empty baselines cannot qualify preservation.

The existing `employee-schema-contract.yaml` workflow has a separately default-off
`include_google_destination_provider` selection. It requires address migration
selection and identical reviewed, published source/control commits. The smallest
combined admission uses `source_sha=H`, `include_address_migration=true`,
`include_public_consumer=true`, `include_google_destination_provider=true`, with
all other optional inputs false. The workflow ref must resolve to that reviewed H;
source SHA alone does not select the updated trusted control workflow.

This keeps the selected 212 assertions (or 341 when journal is explicitly selected)
and generates the full isolated schema once. The existing public compiler fixture
covers CREATE/RESTORE imports; it does not replace migration-specific Web/Utils
compiler and build gates. The Google hook then uses a separate disposable
GoTrue/PostgreSQL fixture on the hosted Linux Docker daemon. It verifies actual
Linux process/daemon context, pulls only the two pinned version images with fixed
time bounds, records their actual IDs, runs one owned process group, and checks
run-bound nonempty preservation/negative-control receipts. The child receives only
needed local tool/Docker environment values; no service/project credentials or
GitHub token are forwarded.

Provider results are recorded in `google-provider.json` in the existing private
schema artifact. The receipt binds source/control H, repository/run/attempt,
fixture UUID, actual image identities, one PUT, preservation counts, process-group
stop and independently observed owned cleanup. Primary or cleanup failure,
unknown inspect outcomes, mismatched output, missing baseline or an upstream
failure leaves a durable unqualified receipt. Finalization cannot turn a prepared
or partially executed receipt into success. No automatic provider retry exists.
The helper removes only exact UUID/name/label-owned resources and verifies absent
containers, network and their volumes. No unrelated Docker cache/resources are
removed. This provider receipt remains distinct from SQL/compiler qualification,
external Google login and hosted/customer outcomes.

The 30-assertion SQL packet also uses an independent local database connection to
hold the precise FK-writer table lock. Preparation must fail NOWAIT with SQLSTATE
55P03, preserve exact mailbox/journal/Auth state, and succeed after that owned
connection is drained. Post-preparation readback verifies the table SHARE fence.
Related ownership/readiness fields remain exact in a grouped JSON assertion;
foundation172, journal301, Google30 and legacy10 counts are unchanged. This uses
`dblink` in the disposable full schema, not a production connection. Executable
source alone is not a passed contention or provider result.

## Explicit retained-mailbox adoption

Empty-only `prepare` keeps rejecting populated placeholders. A separate
`retained-inspect` / `adopt-retained` administrator action supports an unowned,
disabled, unarchived personal canonical mailbox whose sole verified Google
identity belongs to the unchanged legacy account. This action is available in
Infrastructure's address migration dialog after the original tuple is frozen,
including when historical preparation is unknown. It does not resolve that prior
outcome or mint a replacement operation.

The administrator must freshly confirm the exact target UUID, both addresses and
that every retained content item belongs to that account. This is an explicit
entitlement decision for this mailbox snapshot. Missing historical envelope data
remains missing; matching addresses or localparts alone never establish ownership.
The action preserves Auth, complete Google identity, workspace memberships,
mailbox UUID, all retained rows, history and external object references. It makes
no provider request, creates no account, unbans nobody and sends no mail.

The service-only RPC reuses migration authorization and ordered admission locks,
then uses NOWAIT table fences for mail graph DML/DDL and conflicting journals.
It validates the fixed direct and reverse FK inventory, denies unexpected or
composite FKs, and hashes complete retained rows plus linked raw messages,
attachments, recipients and label assignments. Only messages, threads, labels and
stored objects may populate direct mailbox dependencies. Credentials, catch-all
pointers, jobs, historical events, per-user state, notifications and other access
records require separate investigation and block this narrow action. Foreign
authors, cross-mailbox graph links, unlinked/deleted objects, pending or shared
jobs and conflicting employee journals also block it. Whole-mail-table locks make
this a short, bounded administrative transaction, never a bulk import API.

Inspection returns only a snapshot digest and tuple-bound eligibility; it writes
nothing. Adoption revalidates that digest and authorization under the same locks,
then atomically assigns ownership, inserts exactly one owner membership and writes
`private.employee_mailbox_adoptions`. That durable receipt binds the actor,
original operation, revision, target, both addresses and explicit ownership
confirmation. Migration reservation is fenced to that original operation.

Before dispatch, the UI persists an unknown-outcome fence scoped to the actor,
workspace and operation. A lost acknowledgement permits only inspection of the
original receipt. An absent receipt, drift, revoked actor or failed readback never
silently re-enables adoption. A confirmed receipt triggers the ordinary migration
readiness read; reserve/claim/complete remain separate. Clearing browser storage
or choosing another operation is not an unknown-outcome recovery procedure.

Regression coverage is in `employee-retained-mailbox-adoption.sql` (41 assertions, rollback-only
full-schema packet), the adoption session tests and migration HTTP adapter tests.
Run the packet using the canonical isolated Supabase runner with
`--test supabase/tests/employee-retained-mailbox-adoption.sql`, with same-database
`--typegen` output, on the admitted Linux environment. Preserve Studio priority
and cold-restore barriers. Static source checks and mocked HTTP tests do not prove
SQL acceptance; require actual isolated migration application, generated types,
exact-commit CI and independent review before any authorized account operation.
